the synthesized 5,6-halogenated and/or 5,6-oxidized steroidal d-homolactones showed cytotoxic activity against multiple tumor cell lines, with the highest cytotoxicity observed for the 3β-5α, 6β-trihydrate, which was also the most active in the apoptosis study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 5,6-unsaturated d-homo steroid skeleton can be modified to produce compounds with potential anticancer activity, and that the 3β-hydroxy-5,6-oxo and 3β-hydoxy-5,5,6-trioxo derivatives are the most promising candidates for future development.
a number of novel steroidal d-homolactone derivatives were synthesized, and their anticancer potential was evaluated in vitro.
the novel compounds synthesized and evaluated in this study are promising leads for further development of anticancer agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

5,6-epoxidized, halogenated and oxygenated derivatives of 5α-dihydro-5α-hydroxysteroids can be synthesized and are promising anticancer candidates, with the most potent compounds exhibiting cytotoxic activity in the low nanomolar range.
the 5,6-substituted d-homo lactone scaffold is a promising starting point for the development of novel anticancer agents, and that further investigation of these compounds is warranted.
the 3β-hydroxy group and the presence of halogens at the C-5 position and C-6 position of steroidal d-homolactones are important factors for their anticancer properties.
